Its range spans the middle and upper register, and the tone is layered: archaic without losing a clear definition. Because cane is used for the necks and there are several strings, its resonance is distinctive — the hollow body gives a generous resonating chamber, so the sound projects and carries well. Compared with the harp it sounds more primitive and rough; compared with the pipa it is lighter and more transparent. Plucked, it is bright and full of ring, with the warmth and strong rhythmic character typical of African plucked strings.

The pluriarc (also called paata, mapu, luku, kissanga and bow harp) is a string instrument of West Africa, classified as a kind of lute. It has a hollow body and several curved, flexible necks made of cane. The strings run from the necks to a bridge about 1.5 inches (38 mm) from the body. The body may be round, rectangular or triangular and is usually made of light wood. The top of the body may be a separate board fixed by lashing or nails to the lower part, or made from the same wood as the rest of the body.

樂器琴體採用輕木製成，具有良好的共鳴特性。琴頸由蘆葦彎曲製作，提供適當的柔韌性與: The body is made of light wood and resonates well. The necks are bent from cane, which gives the right flexibility and allows the tension to be adjusted. The strings run between the necks and the bridge and may be of animal gut or plant fibre. The bridge, about 38 mm from the body, is usually of wood. The top of the body is a separate board lashed or nailed to the lower part, and the whole design makes full use of the natural materials available in West Africa.
由於多弦弧琴是西非傳統民族樂器，缺乏明確的作曲家署名作品記載。其音樂主要以口頭傳: Because the pluriarc is a traditional West African instrument, there are no clearly attributed works by named composers. Its music is mainly passed on orally and is widely used in the traditional rituals, celebrations and everyday music-making of West African peoples. The related material is mostly preserved as field recordings and ethnomusicological research, such as the West African traditional music archives held by UNESCO.
隨著時間推移，多弦弧琴的製作與演奏技藝在西非各民族間口頭相傳，成為傳統音樂、儀式: Over time the making and playing of the pluriarc were passed on orally among the peoples of West Africa, and it became a central instrument of traditional music, ritual and social life. Its distinctive timbre and expressiveness give it an important place in local musical traditions, and it has continued to shape the development of African string instruments.
